cases.name: composer-2.5-run-2
cases.source: webhook/bench/2026-11-23/runs/composer-2.5/2: the keyword key missed its race

gaps.case: Two deliveries of the same event enqueued while workers are busy can both pass the in-memory Set check before either inserts the id, so the handler runs twice.
Idempotency is keyed on job.eventId from X-Event-Id, but the provider’s canonical event id is the signed JSON body id field; a missing header becomes "" and unrelated deliveries can share one key.
Recording processed only after the handler finishes leaves a failed or partial handler unrecorded, so a provider retry will run the handler again.

approach.reasoning: The planned check-then-handle-then-record flow does not serialize or claim event ids under the existing eight-way concurrent queue, so duplicate deliveries can race past the Set. The dedupe key should come from the signed body id, not the optional header, and the spec needs explicit scenarios for concurrent retries and handler failure before retry.

gaps.case: Two jobs with the same event id can both pass the in-memory set check before either inserts, so the handler runs twice.
The deduplication key comes from the unsigned X-Event-Id header instead of the signed body id.
Provider sends charge.refunded but the only refund handler is registered for refund.created.
Event types without a handler return without being recorded as processed.

rethink.problem: The design checks the in-memory set, runs the handler, and only then inserts the id, so concurrent jobs for the same event id can both execute; adding scenarios cannot make a non-atomic check-then-act sequence atomic.
rethink.alternative: Acquire a lock keyed by the event id around the whole check-handler-insert sequence, or use a database unique constraint to claim the event as processing before the handler and mark it processed after.

approach.reasoning: The core deduplication pattern is racy under the existing concurrent queue, the deduplication key is drawn from an unsigned header, and the provider's refund event type is not handled.

rethink.problem: checking the set before the handler and updating it after allows concurrent deliveries of the same event to both pass the check
rethink.alternative: insert the event id into the database first with a unique constraint

approach.reasoning: The approach relies on an unsigned header that can be missing or spoofed, and its check-then-update logic has a race condition under the queue's concurrency. Adding cases cannot fix the race condition, so the rejected insert-first alternative must be used.

gaps.case: concurrent deliveries of the same event bypass the idempotency check because the set is updated after processing
an attacker replays a webhook with a modified unsigned X-Event-Id header to bypass the idempotency set
the provider sends charge.refunded but the handler expects refund.created, so the refund falls to the fail-open default

rethink.problem: The check-then-act memory set allows race conditions, using an unsigned header allows spoofing, and the fail-open default silently discards mismatched events.
rethink.alternative: Use the signed body 'id' with a database unique constraint for atomic idempotency, and fail closed on unrecognized events to prevent silent data loss.

approach.reasoning: The check-then-act approach allows concurrent duplicates, while using an unsigned header permits replay attacks. Additionally, the fail-open default silently drops essential events like refunds when handler names mismatch, none of which can be fixed simply by adding cases.
